stories.delivered_paragraph: Warner Bros. Discovery has sued Amazon, alleging the company improperly induced executives under fixed-term contracts to leave for Amazon MGM Studios. The complaint centers on former HBO Max marketing executive Pia Barlow, whose Warner contract was due to run through October 31, 2027, and alleges Amazon offered legal protection to employees who breached such deals. The case could test how aggressively California employers can recruit staff bound by term agreements.

stories.delivered_paragraph: TechCrunch has profiled the still-unidentified hacktivist known as Phineas Fisher, who breached two companies that made government spyware. The report portrays Fisher as an unusually prolific figure who publicly embarrassed controversial surveillance vendors while avoiding identification or arrest. The case remains a striking example of how anonymity, leaked data and politically motivated hacking can expose a secretive surveillance industry without resolving who was responsible.

stories.delivered_paragraph: New York’s Flatiron Building is nearing completion of a conversion from offices into ultra-luxury homes, with apartments priced as high as $58.5 million after seven years behind scaffolding. stories.delivered_paragraph: Wildfires have forced more than 300,000 people from homes in France and Spain as high temperatures and strong winds frustrate containment efforts. France ordered another 55,000 evacuations in Gironde and Landes, bringing its regional total to about 250,000, while Spain declared an emergency and confirmed one death in València. Winds are pushing flames toward Bordeaux, leaving firefighters facing what officials say remains an uncontrolled and dangerous fire.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The ACLU honored Bruce Springsteen and former NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick with its new Ralph Ellison Award for Defenders of Civil Rights and Civil Liberties in the Arts, Business, Science and Sports. Kaepernick received the recognition a decade after he began kneeling during the national anthem to protest police violence and racial inequality. Their selection ties cultural prominence and public protest to the ACLU’s broader civil-liberties campaign.
